title: Cold face and head immersion
summary: Entry-level cold via face or brief head immersion—the diving-reflex pathway—practiced as Cold face immersion under Vagus nerve stimulation (3 rounds).

sections.heading: Why face cold is the on-ramp
sections.body: Full-body cold plunges ask for composure, access to water, and recovery bandwidth. Face or brief head immersion is a smaller dose: cold water on the trigeminal territory that can trigger the diving reflex (slower heart rate, breath-hold pattern) without immersing the whole body. It is a practical vagus-adjacent entry and a bridge toward longer thermogenesis work.

sections.heading: Trigeminal cold pathway in plain language
sections.body: Cold on the face activates sensory nerves that feed brainstem circuits linked to the dive response. People often feel a sharp inhale, then a calmer pulse if they stay soft in the shoulders. That autonomic shift is why lifestyle stacks group face cold with other parasympathetic practices. It is not the same as maintaining ~50 °F skin for 10+ minutes on the trunk—that lives under Cold thermogenesis.

sections.heading: How to practice
sections.body: Fill a basin with cool-to-cold water. Start milder (e.g. ~70 °F) and progress cooler as tolerance grows. Dunk the face (eyes optional) for roughly 10–20 seconds; rest about a minute; repeat for 3 rounds—a short, repeatable practice. Morning for alertness or evening for wind-down both appear in community practice; pick one window you will repeat. Breathe calmly between rounds; do not force long breath-holds if you feel panicky.

sections.heading: Where Dr. Jack Kruse’s teaching is specific
sections.body: Kruse’s cold teaching emphasizes thermodynamics and full-body skin targets, but face immersion shows up as an accessible autonomic tool and stepping stone. Community vagus lists often prescribe three rounds. Treat exact timing recipes as teaching culture; treat graded cold on the face as the durable habit before you chase plunge PRs.

sections.heading: What is solid, what is framework
sections.body: Solid ground: facial cold can elicit dive-reflex responses; graded exposure is safer than shock martyrdom; unstable heart disease and cold-triggered conditions need clinician clearance. Framework: that three face dunks equal medical VNS or replace full cold thermogenesis adaptation. Use face cold as Support entry; use the cold-thermogenesis article for heat-engine and ~50 °F skin progression.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Practice Vagus nerve stimulation → Cold face immersion (3 rounds). When ready for shoulders-in water, practice Cold thermogenesis (plunge or shower) with skin temperature and duration. Educational only—not emergency or cardiac care.
